office_does: The sheriff runs the Garfield County Sheriff's Office, the county's law-enforcement agency, which patrols, investigates and serves court process and warrants.
race_blurb: Open seat: Sheriff Drew Hyer is not on the ballot. Deputy and deputies' union president Kristopher Lee Taylor, who led the primary 533 to 415, faces Undersheriff Calvin Dansereau. The office is short-handed: four deputies resigned this summer, during a county hiring freeze.

candidates.summary: Garfield County deputy since 2022, deputies' union president and search and rescue coordinator, running on recruiting and retaining deputies.
highlights: Deputy since 2022; field training officer and search and rescue coordinator [S1]
President of the Garfield County Sheriff's Deputy Union [S1]
Calls retaining qualified deputies one of the office's biggest challenges; would focus on professional growth and local recruiting [S1]

experience.basis: About four years as a deputy, seeking the top job over the sitting undersheriff, on a platform of changing how the office recruits and keeps deputies.

candidates.summary: Garfield County undersheriff for seven years with 17 years in law enforcement, running on leadership experience, accountability and partnerships.
highlights: Undersheriff for seven years; 17 years in law enforcement, including as jail commander [S1][S2]
Eleven years in management before law enforcement [S1]
Says 'public safety begins with strong relationships' and would work with local government and justice partners [S1]

experience.basis: Runs explicitly on 'the leadership, knowledge, and commitment' of 17 years in law enforcement and seven as the office's second-in-command, in both his guide statement and his newspaper profile; not the incumbent sheriff, so not -2.
